image_description: A close-up, high-angle shot of a male mallard duck (drake) floating on calm water. The duck features the characteristic iridescent green head, white neck ring, and grey/brown body plumage. It is facing right, with its head partially out of frame or cropped at the top right. A single brown leaf floats in the water near the duck's reflection.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The duck's head is oriented such that the bill is either completely out of frame or obscured by the angle/cropping. It is not visible for verification.
The eye is located on the side of the head which is largely cropped out or angled away from the camera; it cannot be clearly seen.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible torso exhibits the correct streamlined, buoyant shape typical of a swimming duck. The plumage texture appears dense and consistent with waterproof feathers.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly shows the iridescent green head patch and the distinct white neck ring separating it from the grey/brown body, matching the male mallard description perfectly.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The duck is floating on water; legs and feet are submerged and completely occluded from view.
The folded wing structure is visible along the side of the body. While 'pointed' is hard to judge when folded, the breadth and layering of the flight feathers are anatomically correct.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is visible at the rear left. The characteristic upward curl of the central tail feathers (drake feathers) is clearly present and structurally sound.

artifact_observations.location: Water surface around the duck's body
artifact_observations.reasoning: The water texture immediately adjacent to the duck's hull lacks realistic displacement ripples. It appears slightly smudged or painterly rather than physically interacting with the floating object, suggesting minor generation artifacts in fluid dynamics simulation.

The reflection of the duck's underside and the floating leaf is somewhat inconsistent with the lighting angle. The reflection of the leaf is sharper than the reflection of the duck's body, which violates optical physics for objects at different distances/heights relative to the water plane.
